commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[fray] Correct the L4 and A6000 peak FLOPS (#9574)

Halve the L4 tensor core peaks and stop halving the A6000 fp32 peak, so
both entries store dense peak FLOP/s like the other NVIDIA entries.

The L4 datasheet states that its tensor core figures are "shown with
sparsity" and are half as large without it. The entry stored them
unhalved, so reported MFU on an L4 was half the correct value. L4 bf16
changes from 242e12 to 121e12. L4 fp32 is unchanged at 30.3e12.

The A6000 datasheet marks only its 309.7 TFLOPS tensor figure as using
sparsity. Its 38.7 TFLOPS single-precision figure carries no sparsity
factor, so A6000 fp32 changes from 19.35e12 to 38.7e12.

The A6000 tf32 entry is unchanged. The datasheet gives no TF32 figure,
and the stored value equals the fp16 value. On the A100, A10 and A40 the
TF32 peak is half the FP16 peak, so the stored A6000 tf32 value is
probably twice too large.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[taskcompendium] Add conversation-backed function-call submissions (#9220)

Add a structured model-visible conversation to TaskSpec while keeping
requirements, advertised tools, answer type, and private verifier
separate. Import pinned NeMo next-function-call tasks and support
submission through the final assistant function call alongside plain
text, JSON answers, and submit_answer. The final-call convention
preserves source tool names and arguments; submit_answer carries a text
or numeric answer in its answer argument.

Harbor's ChatAgent normalizes its chat response into typed conversation
evidence and stores the full model-visible conversation, including the
final assistant turn, with decoded function arguments. Malformed
protocol responses fail at the harness boundary with no reward and
retain their raw response for diagnostics. Graders receive the
conversation and Harbor environment, giving them access to environment
state. The predicted-action grader compares submitted final calls with
private expected calls without depending on a harness wire format or
executing them.

Plain-text and JSON submissions preserve advertised functions and their
call policy. The answer-call convention appends submit_answer rather
than replacing task functions. Conflicting call policies and
submit_answer name collisions are rejected before export. This
direct-chat slice captures terminal calls without executing them.

The TaskSpec schema version is now 0.8. Consumers must update their
conversation artifacts and grading calls. Exact, numeric, and
multiple-choice scoring continues to use tasktrove-verify. All 74
package tests pass, including Harbor trials for malformed protocol data
and grading evidence constructed directly without Harbor. Package
Pyrefly and repository lint pass.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
Belay intake: post as a Write-collaborator bot account so transfers reach the locked Belay issue (#9565)

The Belay intake workflow (#9515) has been disabled since #9451 was
locked to collaborators. Only users with write access can comment on a
locked issue. Bot tokens get `403 "Unable to create comment because
issue is locked"`: first the Actions bot (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), then a GitHub
App installation token with `issues: write` (verified on this branch in
[run
36627124129](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/36627124129)).

This PR posts with the token of a dedicated bot account instead:
- **Posting account:** `marin-belay-bot` is an outside collaborator with
the **Write** role on this repo only; it is not an org member, whose
base permission is write on every repo.
- **Its token:** a classic token with only `public_repo`, stored as
`secrets.BELAY_INTAKE_TOKEN`. There's no `workflow` scope, so it can't
edit CI files. Fine-grained tokens are only available to org members.
- **The job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`** now only checks out the repo (`contents:
read`).
- **The transfer script** only trusts transfer markers in comments by
`marin-belay-bot`.

**Verified on this branch** in [run
36630596993](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/36630596993):
the approved test comment on #9514 was copied into the locked #9451
([comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5898834073))
and got a 🚀. A second run will find the marker and copy nothing.

After merge: `gh workflow enable ops-belay-intake.yaml` to turn the
5-minute schedule back on.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Share exact and numeric answer scoring (#9540)

TaskCompendium's direct exact-answer verifier duplicated TaskTrove's
text comparison, and its numeric example graded `12.0` as wrong against
the string `12`. This change lets TaskCompendium use shared TaskTrove
candidate scorers after applying its own plain or JSON submission
convention. TaskTrove's file graders keep their existing boxed-answer
and final-number extraction.

A new `numeric_answer` verifier takes explicit absolute and relative
tolerances. The arithmetic example now grades numeric values, so `12`
and `12.0` agree while nonnumeric content scores zero.
`answer_type=number` still describes the result; the verifier chooses
its grading rule.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Import cleaned TaskTrove MCQA into TaskCompendium (#9216)

Import pinned cleaned TaskTrove MCQA archives as text-answer TaskSpecs.
The importer checks the source answer-line template before replacing its
answer-file and boxed-letter instructions with a one-letter request.
Plain and JSON submission conventions carry that answer; malformed
submissions remain extraction errors.

The importer parses the source `verifier.toml` and stores only its
validated expected letter and option count in the generic `mcq_answer`
verifier. It passes the extracted letter to the shared
`tasktrove-verify` MCQ scorer. TaskTrove's file-based grader uses the
same scorer after parsing its `Answer: X` line, so option-range and
correctness rules have one implementation. The spec records release
provenance. This slice supports MCQ; modes needing private files or
executable graders require an isolated verifier runtime.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Preserve Terminus thinking in normalized chats (#9434)

Extract a leading teacher reasoning span into assistant analysis before
the Terminus JSON command response. The prior adapter discarded that
span. Some AgentTrove GLM-4.6 replies instead wrap the entire command
JSON in `<think>`; unwrap those as final answers. Each source supplies
its reasoning delimiters explicitly, with Penfever selecting them by
cohort. Chats with only plain JSON replies keep thinking disabled.

Malformed leading spans are quarantined. Incidental prose between a
reasoning span and command JSON is still discarded. The affected
chat-processing cache versions are bumped, and each Terminus
processed-chat step hashes its selected delimiters; Penfever OpenCode
partitions retain their cache key. The selected safe tests passed (135
tests). A pinned-source audit tested at least ten raw rows from each of
the 107 Penfever Terminus repositories, AgentTrove, and all four
Nemotron Terminal partitions. Of 1,353 sampled rows, 1,213 produced
structured chat. The AgentTrove sample improved from 13/100 to 95/100
after recovering wrapped command JSON.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
Copy approved Belay intake suggestions into the main Belay issue (#9515)

Marin Belay suggestions now reach the main issue (#9451), and the agent
that acts on it, only after a maintainer approves them. Anyone can post
on the intake issue (#9514). Every 5 minutes this workflow copies each
intake comment that a `marin-devs` member has given a 👍 into #9451, then
adds 🚀 to the original. Approval is checked by numeric GitHub user id,
since a login freed by a rename can be claimed by someone else. A 👍
counts only if it was made after the comment's last edit, so an edited
comment needs a fresh approval.

Copies quote the original, link back to it, and neutralize @-mentions
and HTML-comment syntax. Each copy ends in a hidden marker. Only markers
in the workflow bot's own comments count, so a suggestion can't mark
other comments as already transferred. A later run adds a missing 🚀 if
an earlier run stopped between posting and reacting. To stay within the
`GITHUB_TOKEN` rate limit, full reaction lists are fetched only for
comments that have a 👍 and haven't been copied.

Once this lands, #9451 will be locked so that only users with write
access, plus this workflow, can comment there.

Co-authored-by: ClassicLarry <“larry36d@gmail.com”>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rigging] Speed up telemetry JSON encoding (#9516)

Encode bounded rigging telemetry records with msgspec's sorted JSON
encoder, then enforce the existing byte limit. This removes Python-level
per-chunk encoding from the synchronous emit path. Oversized events
still count as lost without affecting subsequent metric export.

A local arm64 macOS microbenchmark of a 1,060-byte record with 32
attributes measured 114 ms per 5,000 encodes for the prior function and
5.9 ms for msgspec's encoder. This measures encoding, not a MarinSkyRL
stats poll. The affected safe test run passed with 5,603 passed, 10
skipped, and 6 expected failures.

The rigging package declares msgspec, and the root lock records it in
rigging's dependency closure for frozen Iris image installs.
MarinSkyRL's isolated lock pins an older published rigging wheel, so its
runtime needs a later wheel and lock update to receive this change.
